pairs.question: Quis te tantis soluet curis, miseranda, dies?
pairs.answer: Qui me Stygias mittet ad umbras.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels (Nvt., Oc.) and the dangling inline verse number 78. The Nurse asks a genuine interrogative ("what day will free you?"); Octavia answers directly with the relative "the day that will send me to the Stygian shades." Answer is the complete reply (one line, to the full stop); nothing cut.

pairs.question: Quis iste mentes agitat attonitus furor?
pairs.answer: Octauiae fauore percussa agmina et efferata per nefas ingens ruunt.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels (Cho., Nvn.) and inline verse numbers 785 and 787. Chorus asks a real interrogative identifying the madness; the Messenger answers by naming what it is (the troops, struck by favor for Octavia, rushing in fury). Answer is the complete two-line reply to its full stop; nothing further cut.

pairs.question: Quid ausa facere quoue consilio doce?
pairs.answer: Reddere penates Claudiae diri parant torosque fratris, debitam partem imperi.
pairs.derivation: Stripped speaker labels (Cho., Nvn.) and inline verse numbers 788 and 790; normalized the terminal full stop to a question mark. Chorus asks (via doce) what they dared and by what plan; the Messenger answers directly that they prepare to restore Octavia's household gods, her brother's marriage bed, and her owed share of empire. Answer is the complete two-line reply; nothing cut.
